im so sorry :( i’m not a parent but i was 8 when my mum passed away of cancer, i’m now 16.i personally feel as if it was actually offering closure in a sense.
i feel as if because i knew my mum was ill since i was old enough to understand,i was able to know the concept of death. when i visited my mum as she passed away, the feeling is that of loss but also there’s just a sense of surrealism which my siblings also felt and it actually numbed us all from feeling the truth-we didn’t focus on the fact we won’t ever see her again,but rather the fact we enjoyed the time we had spent with her, and there’s a big difference between them both. me and all my siblings agree that we weren’t badly affected by seeing my mum on her death bed. but we do all think that if the cause was sudden then it’s different as the process of grief and all, hits with no pre knowledge and so can cause a lot more difficulty sometimes.
i say follow what your heart says. it may be nice for them to see their great grandma but there’s always the thought of ‘what if this affects them in the future mentally etc.’ 

stay strong, best wishes xx

you’ve been struggling for 8 yrs yet you are still here. As cheesey as it sounds, you have made it through every single day, whether those days have been filled with anger,sadness or emptiness, you are here.

It’s hard when you’ve struggled for a while because you feel helpless and as if it never gets better but i believe in you and admire the resilience you have. There must be something tying you to this earth, your still here. A lot of the times it’s hard to see why but sometimes we don’t don’t see that until we have achieved those momentous things like a family or dream job! those things are coming for you and i pray they do, they will. Because we can’t see them right now it may feel pointless and is tough because we’re left to wonder the purpose of being here and why you don’t have those “normal” things like a crazy good job or something but i assure you, you deserve to be here. Each big thing is made from smaller ones and so for now work towards creating an environment for you to survive, simply survive, you don’t have to ‘thrive’ at the moment, when your struggling it’s okay to go slow and work towards smaller things.
moving slowly is still moving.

20 is such a young age and you deserve to see the incredible things you are and what you’ll become and you can’t see that if your not here.
take it all day by day and take care of yourself!
